newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall for third day in a row.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall for third day in a row.

text.p: French stocks fell on Thursday for a third consecutive session, pressured by the dollar's weakness, a retreat on Wall Street and lower bond prices.

Traders said the market was feeling cautious ahead of the U.S. jobs report for March due out on Friday. They said investors would pay close attention to average hourly wages for signs of any pickup in U.S. inflation.
The blue chip CAC-40 index finished down 15.76 points, or 0.62 percent, at 2,514.52, while the CAC-40 April futures contract fell to 2,501 from 2,527 at Wednesday's close.

Alcatel Alsthom shares fell 4.87 percent to 645 francs, pressured by the sale of three million Alcatel shares placed by brokerage SGE Delahaye. Traders said the paper was absorbed without much difficulty.

Renault shares finished down 1.07 percent at 129.70 francs. The stock slumped more than three percent on a report that a Belgian court ruled that the company breached notification rules when it announced the closure of its Vilvoorde plant. But the stock came off its lows after Renault said the ruling did not affect its intention to close the plant.
